item.description: Sports, countries and tournaments that currently have matches.

description.content:
Returns the hierarchy of the available sports line — sports, their countries and tournaments — with the number of available matches at each level. Use it to build the site menu and to get the `sportId` and `tournamentId` for `events`. It contains no matches or odds.

Only sections that currently have matches for the selected line type are returned, so do not store the IDs as a permanent list. Tournament names may occasionally be empty strings.

**Recommended request frequency:** Live — no more than once every 20 seconds; Prematch (`line`) — no more than once every 60 seconds. See [Data Update Guidelines](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/getting-started/update-guidelines.html).
`true` switches the method to esports data.
(Required) Sports line type: `live` — matches in progress, `line` — upcoming Prematch matches. (This can only be one of live,line)

(Required) Language of names. Use the SportAPI code exactly as listed — some codes differ from ISO (for example `ua`, `cn`, `br`, `al`). The language must also be included in the key's subscription. See [Languages and Language Codes](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/reference/languages.html). request.name: Match list for a sport or tournament

description.content:
Returns matches of the selected sport, grouped by tournament: main match data, teams, start time, Live score and period, a **short** list of the main markets and odds, Live statistics, video and tracker IDs. Use `event` to get the complete market list of one match.

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `.../{sportId}/0/sub/50/line/{lang}` | "Top": 50 matches (next 24 hours first, most popular first) |
| `.../{sportId}/0/sub/50/line/{lang}?match=all` | The full Prematch line of the sport |
| `.../{sportId}/{tournamentId}/sub/50/line/{lang}` | All matches of the tournament |
| `.../{sportId}/0/sub/50/live/{lang}` | All Live matches of the sport |

The "Top" rule does not apply to Live or to esports (`cybersport=true`). In this list `sub_games` and `event_plan` are always `[]`.

**Recommended request frequency:** Live — no more than once every 7 seconds; Prematch (`line`) — no more than once every 30 seconds. See [Data Update Guidelines](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/getting-started/update-guidelines.html).
`true` switches the method to esports data.
`all` — the full line of the sport instead of the "Top" selection. Only for `type=line` with `tournamentId=0`. (This can only be one of all)
`false` returns matches without `game_oc_list`; all other fields are the same and `game_oc_counter` is kept. The response is several times smaller.
(Required) Sport ID taken from a current `menu` or `sports` response for the same line type. See [Sports and `sport_id` Values](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/reference/sports.html).
(Required) Tournament ID taken from a current `menu` or `tournaments` response. Pass `0` to get matches from all available tournaments of the sport.
(Required) Response format. `events` supports only `sub`, which groups matches by tournament. (This can only be one of sub)
(Required) Legacy segment kept for URL compatibility. Always pass `50`: the value does not affect the response and must not be used for pagination.
(Required) Sports line type: `live` — matches in progress, `line` — upcoming Prematch matches. (This can only be one of live,line)

(Required) Language of names. Use the SportAPI code exactly as listed — some codes differ from ISO (for example `ua`, `cn`, `br`, `al`). The language must also be included in the key's subscription. See [Languages and Language Codes](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/reference/languages.html). description.content:
OpenAPI 3.0 description of **SportAPI Sport Line API** — Prematch and Live sports data for
sportsbook websites and applications: sports, countries and tournaments, matches, scores,
Live statistics, betting markets and odds.

This document is written from the public [SportAPI documentation](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/getting-started/quick-start.html)
and covers every documented REST method. It is not an official SDK; when the documentation and this
file disagree, the documentation wins.

## Access

There is no public sandbox. The SportAPI manager gives each client:

- a personal **base URL** (set it as the `baseUrl` server variable);
- a personal **API key**, sent in the `Package` HTTP header with every request — never in the URL.

The key defines the available sports, languages and the access period. See
[Authentication and Access](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/getting-started/authentication-and-access.html).

Every successful response carries the `X-Key-Expires` header with the key's expiration date
(ISO 8601, UTC).

## Core integration flow

```text
menu → events → event
```

1. `menu` — the current hierarchy of sports, countries and tournaments.
2. `events` — matches of a sport or tournament with a short list of the main odds.
3. `event` — the complete market list of one match (or of a sub-match from `sub_games`).

`search`, `sports`, `countries`, `tournaments`, `toplist`, `topmatches`, `topchampionships` and
`account` are additional methods. See [Core Concepts](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/getting-started/core-concepts.html).

## Responses

A response is one of three shapes ([Response Format](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/data-models/response-format.html)):

| Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `status` + `page` + `body` | Data, or an empty result set (`body: []` is not an error) |
| `status` + `page` + `body.message` | State of a specific match in `event` (`Game not found`, `Game id finished`) |
| `error_code` + `error_message` | Access or parameter error |

Check for `error_code` in the parsed JSON instead of relying only on the HTTP status — the
documentation does not define HTTP status codes for error responses. See
[Error Handling](https://sportapi.net/docs/sport-line/getting-started/error-handling.html).

## Live and Prematch

`type=live` returns matches in progress, `type=line` returns upcoming (Prematch) matches. Request
and store them separately: a match that moves from Prematch to Live receives a **new** `game_id`.

## Get an API key

The data API is a commercial service: plans start from $30/month, with a free 2-day trial.
Request a key from the [SportAPI manager on Telegram](https://t.me/sportapinet_bot?start=github_sportapi_openapi) or visit [sportapi.net](https://sportapi.net).
